Loans to overseas subsidiaries rose slightly, reaching $549 million in September. Several companies, including Sun Pharma, led the equity outflows with significant investments.

articles.title: Ather rides to profit; Pronto's US AI play
articles.desc: Ather Energy swung to profit in the July-September quarter. This and more in today’s ETtech Top 5.

articles.title: Anthropic is said to plan public filing for Mega-IPO Monday
articles.desc: Anthropic PBC plans to file for an initial public offering in New York on Monday morning. The artificial intelligence model maker is expected to begin its marketing efforts by November 9. The anticipated IPO aims to rival the size of SpaceX's previous offering, according to industry sources.

articles.title: India-US trade deal enters fine-tuning stage as most talks conclude, says Piyush Goyal
articles.desc: India and the US are refining their bilateral trade agreement after concluding most discussions on the deal. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal indicated significant progress has been made towards finalizing the agreement. Recent talks have involved high-level meetings between officials from both nations, focusing on tariff reductions and trade frameworks. Goyal is currently leading a significant delegation to the Netherlands and Germany to promote bilateral business ties.

articles.title: Exporters get six more months of risk cover amid West Asia turmoil
articles.desc: The Centre has extended the RELIEF initiative to March 31, 2027, to assist exporters. This scheme provides risk coverage to exporters facing higher shipping and insurance costs. Eligible exporters can receive 95 percent coverage and protection against rising insurance premiums. Exporters must submit claims through the Export Credit Guarantee Corporation's customer portal to benefit. The extension aims to support trade flows amid ongoing geopolitical tensions in West Asia.

articles.title: China’s proposed solar technology export curbs may delay India’s domestic manufacturing push: Report
articles.desc: China's plan to impose export controls on photovoltaic technologies could create challenges for India's solar manufacturing sector and affect supply chains. These restrictions may lead to delays and increased costs for domestic players aiming for backward integration in manufacturing. The Approved List of Models and Manufacturers Phase II policy timelines could also be disrupted as a result.

articles.title: Salon owners urge Budget VAT cut as staffing pressures grow
articles.desc: Marcus Perkins, who owns a hair and beauty salon in Brierley Hill, says he is scared for the future.

articles.title: Nirmala Sitharaman reaffirms govt's fiscal discipline push, puts public debt target at 50% of GDP by 2030
articles.desc: FM Sitharaman linked the government's broader economic priorities -- fiscal consolidation, inflation management and currency stability -- with the need to expand employment and enterprise opportunities, particularly for women, through education, skill development and industry participation.

articles.title: Healey to shield low-income pensioners from income tax in the Budget
articles.desc: Changes are needed to prevent the full, flat-rate state pension becoming liable for income tax after it rises in April.

articles.title: How to compare real trading costs across forex trading apps in India
articles.desc: When choosing a forex trading platform, it's important to analyze charges, commissions, and transactional fees. Comparing the overall cost of trade execution is advisable, specifically during peak trading times. For those who trade on the move, testing mobile trading apps for performance and connectivity is vital. Funding and withdrawal charges also affect total expenses, particularly for traders with smaller accounts.

articles.title: US political candidates tailor messages for AI models used by voters
articles.desc: US political candidates have been engineering their campaign messages to appeal to the AI chatbots that more voters have been using to answer questions about issues, and documents seen by Reuters have revealed some of their strategies.

articles.title: Moonshot resets subscriber quotas after Kimi K3.1 Pro launch issues
articles.desc: Chinese artificial intelligence startup Moonshot AI apologised on Monday for rate limiting and unnecessary quota consumption after its Kimi K3.1 Pro launch.

articles.title: India expected to extend duty-free cotton imports through December, sources say
articles.desc: India is expected to extend the 11% customs duty exemption on cotton imports until the end of December to ease supply shortages, lower domestic prices and reduce costs for textile mills. Domestic cotton prices have remained firm amid lower crop prospects, with output estimated below 29 million bales in 2026-27 against demand exceeding 34 million bales.

articles.title: India’s ‘dear friend’ is back in power in Brazil, and a $30 billion trade opportunity is on the table
articles.desc: Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Brazilian President-elect Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election, pledging to deepen the India-Brazil Strategic Partnership. Bilateral trade rose 25% to $15.21 billion in 2025, with Lula setting a target of $30 billion.

articles.title: From Carnegie to Claude: AI wealth could reshape philanthropy
articles.desc: A wave of American wealth created by artificial intelligence companies could produce some of the largest charitable sums since the era of Andrew Carnegie and John D. Rockefeller, raising questions about where the money goes. Nan Ransohoff of payments firm Stripe has described the moment as a "third wave" of American philanthropy, after the industrial fortunes of the late 19th century and the internet billionaires of recent decades.
